translations.text: The word of the Lord that came to Hosea son of Beeri in the days of Ahaz and Hezekiah, in the days of Uzziah and Jotham, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel.

The beginning of the word of the Lord to Hosea. The Lord said to Hosea: "Go and take for yourself a wife of harlotry and children of harlotry, for the land has utterly given itself to harlotry and turned away from the Lord."
So he went and took Gomer, daughter of Diblaim. She conceived and bore him a son.
The Lord said to him: "Name him Jezreel, because in a little while I will avenge the blood of Jezreel on the house of Judah, and I will bring the kingdom of the house of Israel to an end.
On that day I will break the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel."
She conceived again and bore a daughter. The Lord said to him: "Name her Not-Pitied, for I will no longer have mercy on the house of Israel. Instead I will set myself firmly against them.
But I will have mercy on the sons of Judah, and I will save them by the Lord their God. I will not save them by bow or by sword, by warrior or by horsemen."
After she weaned Not-Pitied, she conceived again and bore a son.
And he named him Not-My-People: "For you are not my people, and I am not yours.

Though the number of the sons of Israel be like the sand of the sea, which cannot be counted, only the remnant will be saved. In the place where it was said to them, 'Not my people,' they will be called sons of the living God.
The sons of Israel and the sons of Judah will gather together. They will appoint one ruler over themselves, and they will go up out of the land, for great is the day of Jezreel.
Say to your brother, 'My People,' and to your sister, 'Pitied.'
Bring a charge against your mother, bring a charge, for she is not my wife and I am not her husband. I will remove her harlotries from my sight and her adulteries from between her breasts,
so that I may strip her naked and make her again as she was on the day of her birth. I will make her like a wilderness and set her like a waterless land, and I will kill her with thirst.
I will not have mercy on her children, because they are children born of harlotry.

For their mother played the harlot, and she who bore them brought shame on herself. She said, 'I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread and my water, my clothing and my linen, my oil, and everything I need.'
Therefore I will block [?] her ways with thorns. I will wall up her road, and she will not find her paths.
She will chase her lovers but not catch up with them; [?] nor will she find them. Then she will say, 'I will go back to my first husband, for I was better off then than now.'
She did not realize that it was I who gave her the wheat, the wine and the oil, and who multiplied her silver. But she used the silver and gold for Baal.
Therefore I will turn back and take away my wheat in its season and my wine in its time. I will take my clothing and my linen away from her, so that she cannot cover her shame.
Now I will expose her uncleanness before her lovers, and no one will rescue her from my hands.
I will put an end to all her joys: her feasts, her new moons, her sabbaths and all her assemblies.

And I will ruin her vineyards and her fig trees, of which she said, "These are my wages, which my lovers gave me"; and I will make them a witness, and the beasts of the field and the birds of the sky and the creeping things of the earth shall eat them.
And I will take vengeance on her for the days of the Baals, to whom she sacrificed. She put on her earrings and her necklaces and went after her lovers, but me she forgot, says the Lord.
Therefore, behold, I will lead her astray and make her a wilderness, and I will speak to her heart,
and I will give her possessions back to her from there, and the valley of Achor to open her understanding. And she shall be humbled there, as in the days when she came out of Egypt.
And in those days, says the Lord, she shall call me "My husband" and shall no longer call to the Baals.
And I will take the names of the Baals out of her mouth, and their names shall no longer be remembered.

And in those days I will make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field and the birds of the sky and the creeping things of the earth. I will break the bow and the sword and war from the land, and I will make you dwell in hope.
And I will betroth you to myself forever in righteousness, and in justice, mercy and compassion.
And I will betroth you to myself in faithfulness, and you shall know the Lord.
And in that day, says the Lord, I will hear the sky, and the sky shall hear the earth,
and the earth shall hear the grain and the wine and the oil, and these shall hear Jezreel.

And I will sow her for myself in the land, and I will have mercy on the one who was not pitied. To those who were not my people I will say, "You are my people," and they shall say to me, "You are the Lord my God."
And the Lord said to me again: "Go and love a woman who loves evil and is an adulteress, just as God loves the sons of Israel. Yet they look to foreign idols and love baked cakes of raisins."
And I bought her for myself for fourteen pieces of silver, thirty measures of barley and three mar [?] of wine.
And I said to her, "For many days you shall stay with me. You shall not commit fornication or belong to another husband, and I will be yours."
Therefore the sons of Israel shall stay for many days without a king or a ruler, without offering or altar, without priesthood or revelation.
And after this the sons of Israel shall return and seek the Lord their God and David their king. In the last days they shall be amazed at the Lord and at his good things.
Hear the word of the Lord, sons of Israel, for the Lord has a judgement against the inhabitants of the land. There is no mercy, no truth and no knowledge of the Lord in the land.
Cursing and lying, envy and murder, theft and adultery have spread across the land, and they add blood to blood.

Therefore the land shall mourn and be diminished, together with all who live in it. With the beasts of the land and the creeping things, and with the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea, they shall waste away.
So let no one judge or rebuke, for my people are like a priest who is spoken against.
And you shall grow weak by day, and the prophet too shall grow weak with you by night. I have likened your mother;

My people became like one who had no knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I too will reject you from being my priest. You have forgotten the law of your God, so I too will forget your children.

The more you multiplied, the more they sinned against me. Therefore the land will mourn and be diminished, together with all who dwell in it, with the beasts of the earth and the creeping things. Therefore I set their glory in dishonor.
They eat the sin of my people, and their souls were caught in their falsehoods.
And the priest will be just like the people. I will take vengeance on him and repay him according to his ways.
They will eat and not be satisfied. They will commit fornication and not prosper, because they have forsaken the Lord.
For they went after fornication, and the heart of my people took in wine and drunkenness.
They inquired by joining with one another [?], and with his rods they gave him reports.

They sacrificed on the tops of the mountains and slaughtered offerings on the hills, under the oak and the poplar and the shady trees, because their cover is good. Therefore your daughters will commit fornication and your daughters-in-law will commit adultery.

And I will not look upon your daughters when they commit fornication, or upon your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery, because the men themselves were mingling with harlots and sacrificing with idolaters, and that people, with shaking [?], was mingled with harlots.
But you, Israel, do not be ignorant. And you, Judah, do not go into Gilgal, do not go up to the house of On, and do not swear by the living Lord.
Israel was frenzied like a frenzied heifer. Now the Lord will pasture them like lambs in a broad place.
Ephraim is a partner of idols, and he has laid a stumbling block for himself.
He took pleasure in the Canaanites. They committed fornication over and over, and they loved dishonor from its assembly.
You are a bundle of wind in its wings, and they will be ashamed of its altars.

Hear, O priests, and pay attention, O house of Israel, and let the house of Ephraim listen, for the judgment is against you. You have become a snare to the watchtower, and like a net spread out over [?],
which the hunters of game set firmly in place. But I am your teacher.
I know Ephraim, and Israel is not far from me. For now Ephraim has committed fornication, and Israel is defiled.
They did not apply their thoughts to knowing their God. Instead, a spirit of fornication is among them, and they did not know the Lord.
And the insolence of Israel will be humbled before his face. Israel and Ephraim will grow weak through their falsehoods, and Judah will also grow weak with them.
They will go with sheep and cattle to seek the Lord, and they will not find him. He has turned away from them.
For they have forsaken the Lord, because foreign children have been born to them. Now the fly will devour them and their portions as well.
Blow the trumpet on the hills, cry out on the heights, make a proclamation at the house of On. Benjamin is terrified.
Ephraim has become a ruin in the days of reproof. Among the tribes of Israel I will show what is faithful.
The rulers of Judah have become like people who move boundary markers. I will pour out my onslaught on them like water.
Ephraim overpowered his opponent at law and trampled down justice, because he began to go after vain things.
And I am like a terror to Ephraim, and like a goad against the house of Judah.
In those days Ephraim saw his sickness, and Judah his pain. And Ephraim went to the Assyrians and sent envoys to King Joram. But he will not be able to save you, and the pain will not leave you.
For I am like a panther against the house of Ephraim, and like a lion against the house of Judah. I will go and seize, and there will be no one to rescue.
I will go and return to my own place, until they are destroyed and seek my face.

In their affliction they will rise early and come to me, and they will say, "Come, let us return to the Lord our God, for he has struck us, and he will heal us; he has wounded us, and he will have mercy on us.
He will revive us after two days; on the third day we will rise and live before him.
And let us know him, and let us press on to know the Lord. Like the dawn we will find him ready, and he will come to us like the early rain and the late rain on the earth."
What shall I do to you, Ephraim? Or what shall I do to you, Judah? Your mercy is like a morning cloud, and like the dawn dew that passes away.
Therefore I have mown down your prophets and slain them with the words of my mouth, and your judgment will go forth like light.
For I desire mercy and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than whole burnt offerings.
But they are like a man who transgresses the law.
There Gilead despised me, a city that works vanity and troubles the water.
And your strength is that of a tempter. The priests hid the way; they slaughtered Shechem, for they committed lawlessness.
In the house of Israel I saw there the horrifying fornication of Ephraim. Israel and Judah were defiled.
Begin to gather the grape harvest for yourself when I turn back the captivity of my people.
When I heal Israel, the wickedness of Ephraim and the wickedness of Samaria will be revealed, for they committed falsehood. A thief will come in to strip them, and a robber is on his road,
so that they may make merry together like those who sing praise in their hearts. I have remembered all their wicked deeds. Now their schemes have surrounded them; they were before my face.
With their wickedness they made kings glad, and with their lies, rulers.
They were all committing adultery, like an oven heated for baking, in the heat from the flame, mixed with fat until it has risen.
In the days of your kings the rulers began to rage from wine. He stretched out his hand with the lawless.
For their hearts flared up like an oven, and in their bursting [?] Ephraim was filled with sleep all night. At dawn it flared up like the fire of a furnace.
They all grew hot like an oven and devoured their judges, and all their kings fell, and there was no one among them who called on me.
Ephraim was mixed among his people. Ephraim was like a cake that was not turned over.
And strangers devoured his strength, and grey hairs came upon him, and he did not know it.
And the insolence of Israel will be humbled before his face. And they did not return to the Lord their God, and they did not seek him in all this.
And Ephraim became like a foolish dove that has no understanding. They called on Egypt, and they went into Assyria.
I will cast my net over them, and I will bring them down like the birds of the sky. I will discipline them by the report of their affliction.
Woe to them, for they have strayed from me. They are wretched, for they have acted shamefully toward me. I redeemed them, but they plotted evil against me [?] in return.
And their hearts did not cry out to me, but they wailed on their beds. They cut themselves for wheat and wine.
They were disciplined by me, and I strengthened their arms, yet they plotted evil against me.
They turned to nothing; they became like a slack bow. Their rulers fell by the sword because of the unruliness of their tongue. This is their disgrace in the land of Egypt.
Into their bosom as into the earth [?], like an eagle against the house of the Lord, because they broke my covenant and sinned against my law.
They will cry out to me: "O God, we know you."
For I turned Israel away [?] from the good; they pursued [?] the enemies. They made themselves kings by themselves, and not through me.
They set up rulers and did not let me know. Their silver and gold became idols for themselves, so that they would be destroyed.
Cast away that calf of yours, Samaria! My anger has been kindled against them, until they are unable to be made pure.
In Israel. A craftsman made it, and it is not God, for that calf of yours, Samaria, is a delusion.
For they sowed to a destroying wind, and their ruin awaits them. The standing grain [?] has no strength to yield wheat; and if it does, strangers will devour it.
Israel has been swallowed up. Now they have become among the nations like a useless vessel.
For they went up to the Assyrians. Ephraim sprang up by himself [?]; they loved gifts.
Therefore they were handed over among the nations. Now I will receive them, and they will cease for a little while from anointing [?] (literally "baking") king and princes.
For Ephraim multiplied altars; the beloved altars became sin for him.
And I will write for them righteousness [?], and his statutes were counted as foreign: the beloved altars.

Therefore, if they slaughter a sacrifice and eat the meat, the Lord will not accept it. Now he will remember their lies and take vengeance for their lawless deeds. They will turn back to Egypt, and in Assyria they will eat unclean food.
Israel forgot his Maker and built shrines, and Judah multiplied walled cities. But I will send fire on their cities, and it will devour their foundations.
Do not rejoice, Israel, and do not exult like the other peoples, for you have played the harlot and turned away from your God. You loved the payments of harlotry on every threshing floor of wheat.
The threshing floor and the winepress will not know them, and the wine has deceived them.
They did not settle in the land of the Lord. Ephraim settled in Egypt, and in Assyria they will eat unclean food.

They will not offer wine to him, and their sacrifices will not please him. They will be to them like the bread of mourning, and all who eat it will be defiled. For their bread is for their own hearts [?]; it will not enter the house of the Lord.
What will you do [?] (literally "What will you do me") on the days of assembly, on the days of the Lord's feast?

Therefore, behold, they are going away from the wretchedness of Egypt, and Memphis awaits them, and they buried them at Machmas. Destruction shall inherit their silver, and thorns shall inherit their dwellings.

The days of vengeance are coming, the days of your recompense are coming, and Israel has been made wicked, like a prophet, a man frenzied and filled with a spirit; because of the multitude of your falsehoods, your madness [?] has increased.
Ephraim is a watchman with God; the prophet is a crooked snare in all his ways; they have set up madness in the house of God.
They have become corrupt, as in the days of the hill. He will remember his falsehood; he will take vengeance for his sin.
Like grapes in the desert I found Israel, and like an early watchman of the fig I saw their fathers; but they went in to Baal-Peor and were defiled. They became shameful, like those who were beloved.
Ephraim has flown away like a bird; their glories have flown away, from births and birth-pangs and conceptions.
Therefore, even if they rear their children, they will be made childless among men; for this reason woe to them, for my flesh is from them.
Ephraim, as I saw it as a likeness [?], presented their children as prey, and Ephraim brought out his children to be pierced through.
Give to them, O Lord! What will you give them? Give them a childless womb and dry breasts.
All their wickedness is in Gilgal, for there I came to hate them because of their evil deeds; I will drive them out of my house, and I will no longer love them. All their rulers are rebellious.
Ephraim has been afflicted; his roots have dried up; he will no longer bear fruit. Therefore, even if they give birth, I will kill the beloved offspring of their womb.
God has cast them away, because they did not listen to him, and they will be wanderers among the nations.

Israel is a vine with beautiful branches, its fruit thriving; according to the abundance of its fruit he multiplied altars, and according to the abundance of the good things of his land he multiplied pillars.
Their hearts were divided; now they will be destroyed. He himself will demolish their altars; their pillars have become wretched.
Therefore they will now say: “We have no king, because we did not fear the Lord; and what can a king do for us?”
They speak words on false pretexts; he makes a covenant. Judgment will spring up and grow like couch-grass in a barren field.
The inhabitants of Samaria have become sojourners by the calf of the house of On [Beth-On], for its people mourned over it, and as [?] they had embittered it, they rejoiced over its glory.
For it was carried away from it to Assyria; they bound it and brought it as a gift to King Jarim, to be presented. Ephraim will receive [?], and Israel will be ashamed of its own counsel.
Samaria has cast off its king like a twig on the surface of the water,
and the altars of On, the sin of Israel, will be taken away; thorns and thistles will spring up on their altars, and they will say to the mountains, “Cover us,” and to the hills, “Fall on us.”
From the time that Israel sinned, there they took their stand. War against the children of falsehood will not overtake them on that hill. He came
to chastise them, and peoples will gather against them in their chastisement, for their two falsehoods.
Ephraim is a trained heifer; it loves victory. But I will come upon the best part of its neck; they will come upon Ephraim; I will put Judah to silence; I will strengthen Israel.
Sow righteousness for yourselves; reap the fruit of life. Enlighten yourselves with the light of knowledge. Seek the Lord until the fruit of your righteousness comes.
Why have you kept silent about wickedness and reaped falsehood? For you have eaten the fruit of lies, and you trusted in your chariots and in the great size of your army.

And destruction shall rise up against your people, and all your fortified places shall be gone, as the ruler Salaman was destroyed by the house of Jeroboam. In the days of battle they dashed the mother down upon her children.
So will I do to you, O house of Israel, because of your wickedness.
At dawn they were cast off; the king of Israel was cast out. For Israel was an infant, a child, and I loved him, and out of Egypt I called his children.
As I called them, so they went away from my presence. They sacrificed to the Baals and burned incense to carved images.
I hobbled Ephraim; I took him up in my arms, and they did not know that I heal them.
In the corruption of men I drew them along with the bonds of love, and I will be to them like a man who strikes their cheek, and I will look upon him.
Ephraim settled in Egypt, and the Assyrian is his king, because he would not turn back.
And the sword in his scabbards grew weak and came to rest in his hands, and they shall eat the fruit of their own schemes.
And his people hang from his dwelling place. God shall be angry at his honour and shall not exalt him.

What shall I promise you, Ephraim? Shall I help you, Israel? What shall I promise you? I will make you like Admah and like Zeboiim. My heart is turned over within me all at once; my repentance is shaken.
I will not act according to the wrath of my anger. I will not let Ephraim be wiped out, for I am God and not a man among you, and I will not enter the city.
I walked after the Lord, as a lion was roaring, for they were committing adultery, and the offspring of the waters shall be terrified.
[?] like birds from Egypt and like doves from the land of Assyria, and I will bring them back again to their homes, says the Lord.
Ephraim has surrounded me with lies, and the house of Judah with ungodliness. Now God has known them, and they shall be called the holy people of God.
But Ephraim chased an evil wind, the scorching heat. Every day he increased emptiness and vanity. He made a covenant with the Assyrians and went in to seek favour.
And the Lord's judgement is on Judah, to take vengeance on Jacob. He will repay them according to his ways and according to his deeds.
In the womb he supplanted his brother, and through his labour he grew strong against God.
And he grew strong against the angel and overcame him. They wept and pleaded with me. They found me in my house, and there it was said to him:
"But the Lord God Almighty shall be his memorial."
And you, turn back to your God. Keep mercy and justice, and draw near to your God always.
Canaan: in his hand is the yoke of falsehood; he has loved domination.
Ephraim said, "Now I have become rich; I have found rest for myself." But his labours shall not be found for him, because he sinned through falsehood.
I am the Lord your God, and I brought you out of the land of Egypt, and I will yet again make you dwell in tents, as on the day of a feast,
And I spoke to the prophets, and I multiplied visions, and by the hands of the prophets I was represented in likenesses.
If it is Gilead, were they false to me? In Gilgal the rulers were sacrificing, and their altars were like turtles on the dry land of the field.
And Jacob withdrew into the plain of Syria, and Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept watch.
And by a prophet the Lord brought Israel up out of the land of Egypt, and by a prophet he was kept.
Ephraim set his heart to anger and provoked wrath; and his blood shall be poured out upon himself, and the Lord shall repay him his reproach.
According to the word of Ephraim, he took his statutes in Israel, and he laid them down for Baal, and he died.

And they added to their sin, and made for themselves an idol from their silver by melting it, in the image of an idol, the work of craftsmen, finished by them. And they say: Slaughter men, for meat has run short.
Therefore they shall be like the clouds of morning, and like the dew of dawn that passes away, and like dust from the threshing floor, and like a vapor of tears.

I am the Lord your God, who established the heaven and created the earth, whose hands made all the hosts of heaven; and I did not show them to you so that you should go after them and follow them. And I brought you up out of the land of Egypt; and you did not know a god besides me, and there is no savior apart from me.
I shepherded you in the uninhabited land, in the wilderness,
according to their pastures; and they were filled to fullness, and their hearts were exalted, and therefore they forgot me.
And I became to them like panthers, and like a leopard on the road of the Assyrians.

I will meet them like a distraught bear, and I will tear open the enclosure of their heart; and the whelps of the thicket shall devour them there, and the wild beasts of the field shall tear them apart.
In your destruction, Israel, who will help you?
Where is that king of yours? Let him save you in all your cities; let them judge you, of whom you said: Give me a king and a ruler.
And I gave you a king in my wrath, and I held him in my anger.
Ephraim is a gathering of falsehood; his sin is hidden away.
Pangs like those of a woman giving birth shall come upon him. This is your wise son, for they could not withstand the crushing of the children.
From the hand of Hades I will deliver them; from death I will rescue them. Now where is your judgment, O death? Where is your sting, O Hades? Comfort is hidden from my eyes.

For he will cause division among brothers. The Lord will bring a burning wind upon them from the wilderness, and it will dry up their outflowing streams and ruin its springs. It will dry up its land and all its desirable vessels.
Samaria shall be made to vanish, for she rose up against her God. Their fornications have fallen by the sword; they were dashed to the ground, and their pregnant women were ripped open.
Return, Israel, to the Lord your God, for you have grown weak in your falsehoods.

Take words with you and return to the Lord your God. Say to him: You have the power to forgive sins, so that you may not receive falsehood but may receive good; and we will render the fruit of our lips.
Assyria will not save us; we will no longer mount horses, nor will we say: Our gods are the works of men's hands. He who is among you will have mercy on the orphan.
I will heal their dwelling; I will love them.
And I will be like dew to Israel; he will blossom like the lily, and his roots will spread out like Lebanon.
His branches will go forth, and he will be like a fruitful olive tree, and his fragrance will be like that of incense.
They will return and sit under his shelter; they will live on wheat, they will be strengthened and will blossom. His memorial will be like a vine, and like the wine of Lebanon
of Ephraim. What more has he to do with idols? I will humble him, and I will strengthen him. I am like a [?] fir tree; from me your fruit is found.
Who is wise and will understand these things, and prudent and will know them? For the ways of the Lord are straight, and the righteous will walk in them, but the ungodly will grow weak in them.
